articles.title: Ciro Fernandes celebra xilogravura entregue a Leonardo DiCaprio | G1
articles.standfirst: A obra 'São Jorge', do paraibano Ciro Fernandes, foi dada como um presente ao ator e ativista norte-americano pela ministra da Cultura, Margareth Menezes.
articles.summary: A obra 'São Jorge', de Ciro Fernandes, foi entregue a Leonardo DiCaprio pela ministra Margareth Menezes como um símbolo da riqueza da arte popular brasileira.
articles.body:
Obra 'São Jorge' produzida pelo artista paraibano Ciro Fernandes — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

O artista paraibano Ciro Fernandes celebrou a entrega da obra "São Jorge" ao ator e ativista norte-americano Leonardo DiCaprio . A xilogravura foi dada durante a visita do artista ao Brasil como um presente, na última quarta-feira (2), pela ministra da Cultura, Margareth Menezes, em encontro no Palácio do Planalto.

Ao g1 , Ciro Fernandes afirmou que foi uma surpresa muito grande. O artista só soube da entrega da obra por meio de publicação no jornal O Globo.

O xilogravador, que já fez diversas obras e cartazes de cinema no Brasil, celebrou a entrega do presente.

"É uma honra muito grande. Ainda mais uma figura que tem uma representatividade universal. Me sinto muito honrado e muito feliz", disse.

Ciro Fernandes, artista paraibano responsável pela obra entregue a Leo DiCaprio. — Foto: Divulgação/Ciro Fernandes

Na xilogravura, São Jorge, o santo guerreiro, é representado com um chapéu de Lampião, comum no Nordeste, de onde é a origem do artista. Além disso, a representação do santo luta contra um dragão de três cabeças, figura mística comum no cordel.

A obra faz parte do Clube de Colecionadores do Museu do Pontal, no Rio de Janeiro . Em uma publicação nas redes sociais, a ministra Margareth Menezes ressaltou a identidade brasileira por meio da arte popular. "Um verdadeiro tesouro da nossa identidade, que preserva a genialidade da arte popular brasileira", escreveu.

Margareth Menezes entrega obra de artista paraibano como presente a Leonardo DiCaprio — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

O filho e diretor de arte de Ciro, Bruno Fernandes, explicou que as obras do artista são criadas a partir do que ele observa, como gatos, bois, trabalhadores e bairros do Rio de Janeiro, cidade onde mora, e que possuem uma representatividade brasileira muito forte, do Nordeste ao Sul.

"Ele retrata realmente muitos elementos sertanejos. Ele nasceu no Alto Sertão, onde a nossa família conviveu com Lampião. Isso aí é retratado na arte dele. É uma forma de perpetuar a raiz dele. Mas ele retrata o Brasil como um todo. A arte dele é figurativa e ele desenha tudo que vê, principalmente o cotidiano das pessoas", explicou.

Ciro Fernandes nasceu em Uiraúna , no sertão da Paraíba. Começou a desenhar em madeiras e nas paredes da casa dos avós durante a infância. Ele deixou a Paraíba em 1958, aos 16 anos.

O artista trabalhou como cobrador de ônibus, soldador mecânico, operário e pintor de paredes. Ele ocupou o cargo de diretor de arte em agências de publicidade e foi ilustrador do Jornal do Brasil e O Globo. Também ilustrou livros de autores e capas de discos de artistas brasileiros.

Atualmente Ciro tem um ateliê na Lapa, no Rio de Janeiro, e as obras dele fazem parte de acervos, como o do Museu Nacional de Belas Artes.

articles.title: What are the implications of AfD’s electoral rise for Germany and Europe?
articles.summary: The far-right Alternative for Germany is just short of a majority in a regional election.
articles.body:
Early results show the Alternative for Germany finished on top in Sunday’s election in the east German state of Saxony-Anhalt, with about 44 percent of the vote. The AfD is now close to becoming the first far-right party to lead a German state since World War II. It’s benefitted from voters’ economic concerns and increasing anger over immigration.

The party is also leading in national polls. But Germany’s domestic intelligence agency has classified its branch in Saxony-Anhalt as a proven right-wing extremist group – a label the AfD has rejected. Chancellor Friedrich Merz insists there can be no co-operation with the AfD, and mainstream German parties have been maintaining a ‘firewall’ against forming coalitions with the far-right. But it’s not clear if the strategy will hold.

So, what does the AfD’s rise mean for Germany – from its immigration policy to its role in Europe?

Olaf Boehnke – Berlin Director of the political consultancy Rasmussen Global and former Senior Advisor in the German Bundestag

Max Otte – Founder of Privatinvestor Capital and a 2022 German presidential candidate

Ulrich Brueckner – Professor of European Studies at Stanford University in Berlin

articles.title: Com assassinato de mãe de três filhos, região de Campinas chega a 15 feminicídios em 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Morte de Talita Ramos Andrade, de 35 anos, em Artur Nogueira elevou para 15 o número de casos registrados neste ano; em 13 deles, os suspeitos eram parceiros ou ex-parceiros das vítimas.
articles.summary: Morte de Talita Ramos Andrade, de 35 anos, em Artur Nogueira elevou para 15 o número de casos em 2026; em 13 deles, os suspeitos eram parceiros ou ex-parceiros das vítimas.
articles.body:
Com o assassinato de Talita Ramos Andrade, de 35 anos, mãe de três filhos encontrada morta em uma estrada rural de Artur Nogueira (SP), a região de Campinas chegou a ao menos 15 casos de feminicídio registrados em 2026.

O suspeito do crime é Anderson Souza Andrade Ramos, de 42 anos, ex-companheiro da vítima. Ele foi baleado e preso após ser encontrado escondido debaixo de um galinheiro , na região do Jardim Blumenau, nesta segunda-feira (7).

O levantamento mostra que a violência contra a mulher permanece concentrada principalmente no ambiente doméstico.

Em 13 dos 15 casos registrados neste ano, o suspeito era marido, companheiro ou ex-companheiro da vítima.

Talita Ramos Andrade foi encontrada morta em estrada rural de Artur Nogueira — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Talita havia se mudado de Artur Nogueira após o fim do relacionamento com Anderson. Ela vivia em Campinas por medo de ameaças e para recomeçar a vida, segundo a família.

A vítima possuía medida protetiva contra o ex-companheiro e havia registrado, neste ano, um boletim de ocorrência em que relatou ser alvo constante de ameaças.

Campinas lidera o número de ocorrências, com quatro feminicídios em 2026, seguida por Hortolândia , com três. Veja os números:

16 de janeiro: Letícia Chaves de Oliveira, de 26 anos, foi morta a tiros dentro de casa , no bairro Samambaia, em Valinhos (SP). O marido, Maicon César Ferreira, foi preso no mesmo dia. A vítima foi baleada na frente dos filhos, de 11 e 4 anos .

22 de janeiro: Yasmin Evely da Silva, de 25 anos, foi espancada e esfaqueada até a morte pelo marido no Jardim Nova Esperança I, em Sumaré (SP). Diego Molino da Silva fugiu após o crime, mas foi localizado e preso em Hortolândia. A investigação apontou que ele monitorava a vítima por meio de uma câmera instalada na residência.

30 de janeiro: Naiara Souza Lopes, de 33 anos, foi morta a facadas dentro de casa , no bairro Sacilotto, em Artur Nogueira. O ex-marido da vítima, Ricardo Machado de Souza, que não aceitava o fim do relacionamento e se entregou à polícia semanas depois . O filho do casal, de 3 anos, teria presenciado o crime.

2 de fevereiro: Rita de Cássia da Silva Coura, de 48 anos, foi encontrada morta dentro da casa onde vivia , no Jardim Campos Elíseos, em Campinas. O companheiro foi preso e a família relatou um histórico de agressões ao longo do relacionamento de cerca de 30 anos.

2 de fevereiro: Ana Paula Perpétuo, de 41 anos, foi morta a marretadas dentro de casa, na região central de Lindóia. O marido, José Edson Gonçalo dos Santos, confessou o crime e foi preso pela Guarda Municipal.

14 de março: Julyene de Lima dos Santos, de 27 anos, foi morta a facadas na Rua Guarujá, no Jardim Europa, em Hortolândia. O principal suspeito, o companheiro José Felipe Pereira de Souza, foi localizado dias depois e preso pela Guarda Municipal de Vinhedo .

29 de abril: Carla Viviane da Silva, de 28 anos, morreu após ser atingida por um tiro dentro da própria casa , em Hortolândia. O companheiro, Hendryo Arnobio de Araujo Santos, foi preso. Segundo a investigação, o casal discutia quando ele pegou uma arma para ameaçá-la. A vítima deixou dois filhos, de 7 e 9 anos.

1º de maio: Vanessa Oliveira dos Santos, de 19 anos, foi morta com golpes de martelo e facadas em um apartamento no Parque Progresso, em Itapira. Dois homens foram presos em flagrante pelo crime.

9 de maio: Najylla Duenas Nascimento, de 34 anos, foi morta a tiros pelo companheiro , o guarda municipal Daniel Barbosa Marinho, durante a festa de casamento do casal, em Campinas. Após fugir, ele retornou ao local e se entregou. A vítima deixou três filhos .

1º de junho: Jaciara Lima, de 45 anos, foi morta a facadas pelo companheiro dentro da residência do casal, no Residencial Olímpia, em Campinas. Segundo a polícia, o crime ocorreu durante uma discussão. Após matar a vítima, o homem tirou a própria vida.

12 de junho: Fabiola Batista Dias, de 31 anos, mulher trans, morreu após ser agredida por um homem com quem mantinha relacionamento , na Vila Vitória, em Campinas. O suspeito foi preso em flagrante.

8 de agosto: Eliane do Carmo Pereira, de 42 anos, foi morta a facadas dentro de casa , no bairro Ana Carolina, em Valinhos. O marido, Márcio de Souza Milani, tentou se matar após o crime e permaneceu internado sob escolta policial. A vítima havia registrado ameaças anteriormente.

9 de agosto: Elinalva Mendes Teixeira Pacheco, de 35 anos, foi encontrada morta com golpes de faca dentro de casa , no Jardim Campo Belo, em Campinas. O companheiro, Antônio Rocha, foi preso em Goiás dias depois . A polícia descobriu que ele tinha histórico de violência contra outras mulheres.

4 de setembro: Cleonice Aparecida Pinheiro de Oliveira, de 54 anos, foi morta a facadas dentro de casa , no Jardim Minda, em Hortolândia. O companheiro, Cristiano Ribeiro, foi preso em flagrante por feminicídio.

5 de setembro: Talita Ramos Andrade, de 35 anos, foi encontrada morta em uma estrada rural de Artur Nogueira. Ela tinha medida protetiva contra o ex-companheiro, Anderson Sousa Andrade Ramos. A Justiça decretou a prisão preventiva dele, que foi baleado e preso após buscas em uma região de mata .

articles.title: Juliana Brizola defende subsídio para o transporte escolar no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidata ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul pelo PDT cumpriu compromissos de campanha em Porto Alegre.
articles.summary: Candidata ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul pelo PDT cumpriu compromissos de campanha em em Porto Alegre.
articles.body:
Candidata ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul pelo PDT, Juliana Brizola cumpriu compromissos de campanha nesta segunda-feira (7). Ela esteve em Porto Alegre .

No Parque Farroupilha, conhecido como Parque da Redenção, gravou materiais para TV, rádio e redes sociais. Junto a apoiadores, tirou fotos com eleitores que passavam pelo parque. Neste 7 de Setembro, a candidata também realizou reuniões internas com aliados e gravou outros conteúdos em estúdio.

Até o dia 2 de outubro, os candidatos ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul vão responder perguntas feitas diretamente por eleitores entrevistados pela RBS TV. Serão seis temas, um a cada semana: segurança, saúde, educação, infraestrutura, economia e prevenção a desastres climáticos . Ao todo, 86 eleitores terão suas dúvidas respondidas .

Os candidatos terão 30 segundos para apresentar suas respostas. Dos sete candidatos, três responderão em cada dia . A ordem de aparição leva em conta a mais recente pesquisa eleitoral contratada pelo Grupo RBS , divulgada nesta segunda-feira (24).

Sobre educação , a candidata escolheu a pergunta da eleitora Natália, de Bagé, na região da Campanha. "Gostaria de saber o que vão fazer para melhorar o transporte escolar do estudante" , questiona.

"Infelizmente, o estado não vem cumprindo com o mínimo constitucional para a educação. Isso provoca, na verdade, uma crise em vários setores dentro da educação. Um deles é o próprio transporte escolar. Então, precisamos subsidiar esse transporte, sobretudo no Interior, nas nossas escolas rurais. E esse será o meu compromisso. Transporte de qualidade e seguro para as nossas crianças", afirmou Juliana.

Juliana Brizola cumpriu compromissos de campanha em Porto Alegre nesta segunda-feira (7) — Foto: Reprodução/RBS TV

articles.title: João Campos promete incluir adultos em centros TEA estaduais | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PSB ao governo de Pernambuco cumpriu agenda de campanha no bairro do Poço da Panela, na Zona Norte do Recife, nesta segunda-feira (7).
articles.summary: Candidato do PSB ao governo de Pernambuco cumpriu agenda de campanha no bairro do Poço da Panela, na Zona Norte do Recife, nesta segunda-feira (7).
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo de Pernambuco João Campos ( PSB ) cumpriu agenda de campanha em seu comitê de campanha no Poço da Panela, na Zona Norte do Recife , nesta segunda-feira (7). Ele prometeu estender o atendimento dos centros estaduais de Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA) para jovens e adultos, além de lançar um programa específico de empregabilidade.

Ele cumprimentou e tirou fotos com apoiadores. O evento, intitulado "Encontro da Inclusão", reuniu famílias, entidades e institutos que atuam no suporte a pessoas com deficiência e neurodivergência para sugerir diretrizes para políticas públicas.

O encontro também contou com a presença do candidato a vice-governador na chapa, Carlos Costa (Republicanos). Durante a agenda, João Campos reforçou seus planos de fortalecer a educação inclusiva para estudantes com TEA e outras condições do neurodesenvolvimento e detalhou o plano para assegurar o atendimento especializado a essas famílias.

"Nos centros TEA estaduais, que vão atender pessoas com deficiência, com neurodvergência, também vão atender jovens e adultos, no caso do estadual. E a gente vai ter um programa específico para empregabilidade, para ajudar a aproximação com o mercado de trabalho e garantir a formação e a presença dessas pessoas no mercado formal de trabalho", afirmou.

articles.title: Virginia e Zé Felipe celebram 2 anos de José Leonardo em Goiânia | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor e influenciadora celebraram o aniversário do filho caçula. A festa temática do Homem-Aranha contou com detalhes como teto iluminado e opções de doces sem açúcar.
articles.summary: Virginia e Zé Felipe celebraram os 2 anos de José Leonardo com festa do Homem-Aranha em Goiânia, trazendo decoração iluminada e opções de doces sem açúcar.
articles.body:
O cantor Zé Felipe postou um vídeo mostrando a chegada ao aniversário de 2 anos do filho caçula, José Leonardo, ao lado da influenciadora Virginia Fonseca e das filhas Maria Flor e Maria Alice. A festa foi preparada com o tema do Homem-Aranha e doces sem açúcar. Aniversariante e as irmãs mais velhas chegaram com fantasias do super-héroi.

No vídeo compartilhado pelo cantor, ele e Virginia vestem roupas vermelhas e se revesam para segurar o filho José Leonardo e as filhas mais velhas. As crianças vestem roupas do Homem-Aranha, combinando com a decoração do espaço.

Na tarde desta segunda-feira (7), a influenciadora compartilhou stories mostrando a decoração para a festa e destacou o teto com uma teia iluminada e o boneco do super-herói em uma das poses mais clássicas dos quadrinhos, pendurado de cabeça para baixo.

Zé Felipe com o filho José Leonardo (centro) e Virgínia Fonseca — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram Zé Felipe

Outro ponto que chama a atenção é que, no espaço, os convidados vão encontrar doces sem açúcar. De acordo com Virginia, as sobremesas vão ficar em uma kombi. "Nessa festa eu lembrei de pedir doces sem açúcar e vai ficar bem aqui" , escreveu Virgínia, mostrando o lugar onde os convidados vão encontrar as sobremesas.

articles.title: Olinda abre temporada de prévias de carnaval com desfile da Pitombeira | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao som de muito frevo, multidão acompanhou desfile, que saiu às 16h30 desta segunda (7).
articles.summary: Ao som de muito frevo, multidão acompanhou desfile, que saiu às 16h30 desta segunda (7).
articles.body:
Faltam mais de 150 dias para o carnaval de 2027, mas, em Olinda , a festa já começou. Nesta segunda-feira (7), cidade deu início oficial às prévias carnavalescas, e as ladeiras do Sítio Histórico ficaram lotadas de foliões e folionas ansiosos pela folia (veja vídeo acima) .

O cortejo saiu pontualmente às 16h30, com um desfile histórico da Pitombeira dos Quatro Cantos. A agremiação de quase 80 anos arrastou uma multidão que, ao som da Orquestra do Maestro Babá, matou a saudade dos pernambucanos e até de quem cruzou o Oceano Atlântico para cair no frevo.

Um exemplo é o da gerente de restaurante Francisca Fritz, que é austríaca e veio para Pernambuco bem na época em que começam as prévias.

"Eu vim para conhecer Pernambuco e felizmente caiu na abertura do carnaval, as prévias. Eu tive férias agora, nessa época, e caiu certo. É uma energia muito massa, muito legal aqui", contou.

Francisca Fritz veio da Áustria para brincar na abertura do carnaval de Olinda — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

E quando se diz que o olindense está "contando os dias" para o carnaval, não é exagero. O advogado Sérgio Barreto, por exemplo, é famoso por sair pelas ladeiras com uma placa informando, na Quarta-feira de Cinzas, quantos dias faltam para a folia do ano seguinte.

"Há mais de 30 anos tive essa ideia de fazer a contagem, e tive o prazer e a sorte de, em 2023 ser homenageado pelo Homem da Meia-Noite como o 'Homem do Tempo'. O homem que sai do carnaval contando os dias para o próximo", contou o folião.

Em 7 de setembro, na abertura das prévias, placa mostra contagem do tempo até o carnaval de Olinda 2027 — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Foi a Pitombeira dos Quatro Cantos que, há 26 anos, oficializou a abertura das prévias, sempre com um desfile no Dia da Independência do Brasil. Segundo Hermes Neto, presidente da troça, para celebrar os 80 anos do grupo, que ocorre em 17 de fevereiro, uma camisa especial vai ser lançada, celebrando também o sucesso da indumentária no filme "O agente secreto", indicado a quatro categorias do Oscar .

"Espero que o carnaval esse ano tenha muita paz. Estou sentindo que, realmente, a gente montou um grande desfile, porque o público está comparecendo. O filme ['O agente secreto'] nos ajudou bastante, apesar da nossa história já ser muito rica no carnaval. Mas o filme colocou a gente em muitos países", contou.

articles.title: Forças de Israel matam 12 pessoas, incluindo 2 crianças, no Líbano | G1
articles.standfirst: Testemunha disse que um dos ataques atingiu um prédio residencial no momento em que as crianças se preparavam para ir à escola. Israel alega ter atacado pessoas vistas transferindo armas na região da cidade de Kfar Rumman.
articles.summary: Testemunha disse que um dos ataques atingiu um prédio residencial no momento em que as crianças se preparavam para ir à escola.
articles.body:
Israel bombardeia cidade no sul do Líbano em 7 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: Karamallah Daher/Reuters

Ataques israelenses a uma cidade no sul do Líbano mataram pelo menos 12 pessoas, incluindo duas crianças, na manhã desta segunda-feira (7), informou o Ministério da Saúde do Líbano, marcando um dos dias mais letais de bombardeios israelenses nas últimas semanas.

Crescem no Líbano os temores de uma nova campanha militar israelense, após dias de escalada nos ataques, apesar de um cessar-fogo estabelecido em junho que visava interromper os combates entre o exército de Israel e o grupo armado libanês Hezbollah.

Uma mulher, que afirmou ser parente de pelo menos três das vítimas, disse que um dos ataques atingiu um prédio residencial no momento em que as crianças se preparavam para ir à escola. O exército israelense declarou ter atacado pessoas vistas transferindo armas na região da cidade de Kfar Rumman.

No local, repórteres da Reuters viram livros escolares espalhados entre blocos de concreto, onde antes ficava o prédio. Equipes de resgate, utilizando maquinário pesado, trabalharam durante toda a manhã para retirar corpos debaixo dos escombros.

Mustafa Farhat, de oito anos, perdeu os avós e a mãe no ataque, segundo moradores locais. Na manhã de segunda-feira, equipes de resgate ainda buscavam o corpo de seu pai, enquanto o menino recebia tratamento hospitalar para seus ferimentos, acrescentaram.

Uma de suas parentes, Mona Farhat, disse à Reuters que a casa da família foi atingida pouco antes do horário de ir para a escola.

"O que eles atacaram? Qual é o objetivo deles? Querem que deixemos nossa terra? Estão enganados", disse Farhat no hospital.

O Ministério da Saúde do Líbano informou que 11 pessoas — incluindo duas crianças e quatro mulheres — morreram no ataque ao prédio residencial na segunda-feira. A mídia estatal havia noticiado anteriormente que o ataque ocorreu após a meia-noite.

Um ataque separado realizado por um drone israelense contra um veículo civil na cidade matou um socorrista , segundo o Ministério da Saúde. Outros dois socorristas ficaram feridos na ação, informou a pasta.

Os ataques a Kfar Rumman ocorreram sem que houvesse um aviso prévio de evacuação online por parte do exército israelense.

As forças de Israel afirmaram que medidas foram tomadas para mitigar danos "a indivíduos não envolvidos, incluindo o uso de munições de precisão e vigilância aérea".

As forças armadas declararam estar analisando o relato de que "indivíduos não envolvidos" foram feridos em decorrência dos ataques. As forças armadas de Israel informaram que o Hezbollah lançou dois drones explosivos durante a noite contra tropas israelenses que operavam perto da crista de Ali al-Taher, um conjunto estratégico de colinas no sudeste do Líbano onde se acredita que o Hezbollah tenha construído um complexo militar subterrâneo.

Israel afirmou na semana passada que havia expulsado os combatentes do Hezbollah do local. O Hezbollah não se pronunciou, e a Reuters não conseguiu confirmar de forma independente a situação militar em Ali al-Taher.

Nos dias seguintes, Israel intensificou ataques letais contra cidades ao norte e a oeste da crista, para onde os moradores haviam retornado após o cessar-fogo de junho, disseram autoridades de segurança libanesas à Reuters.

As autoridades afirmaram prever uma escalada contínua no sul nas próximas semanas.

No domingo, pelo menos 11 pessoas morreram em ataques israelenses contra três cidades próximas ao local, segundo um balanço atualizado do Ministério da Saúde do Líbano.

O Ministério da Saúde informou que ataques israelenses distintos, ocorridos no domingo, destruíram o hospital Ghandour, na cidade de Nabatieh al-Fawqa.

Outras quatro pessoas morreram na sexta-feira, incluindo uma mulher, acrescentou a pasta. Esses ataques ocorreram sem avisos de evacuação.

Os ataques israelenses ao Líbano mataram mais de 4.300 pessoas desde que o Hezbollah disparou foguetes contra Israel em 2 de março — dois dias após o início dos ataques dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã —, desencadeando uma ofensiva aérea e terrestre israelense.

Entre os mortos estão mais de 250 crianças, quase 400 mulheres e mais de 130 profissionais de saúde, segundo o Ministério da Saúde do Líbano. O ministério não faz distinção entre civis e militantes, e o Hezbollah não divulgou um balanço de baixas de seus próprios combatentes.

O cessar-fogo levou a uma redução drástica da violência, mas as tropas israelenses que ocupam áreas do sul do Líbano continuaram a destruir vilarejos na autoproclamada zona de segurança. Os militares israelenses prosseguiram com ataques tanto dentro da zona quanto ao norte dela, na maioria das vezes sem emitir avisos de evacuação.

articles.title: Police hunt launched after man killed in hit-and-run near Edinburgh Airport
articles.summary: A Police dog unit and helicopter are involved in the search for three people who left the scene of the crash on foot.
articles.body:
Police are searching for two women and a man who fled on foot from the scene of a fatal hit-and-run crash on the A8 near Edinburgh Airport.

Officers were called to reports of a crash involving a grey Mercedes A250, a black Renault Captur, a grey Skoda Karoq and a grey Hyundai i30 between the Newbridge and Gogar roundabouts at around 09:25 on Monday.

Emergency services attended, however, the 58-year-old driver of the Hyundai i30 was pronounced dead at the scene.

A police helicopter and dog unit have been used to hunt for the three people who left the scene.

Four others were taken to hospital for treatment following the crash but they were later released.

Insp Thomas Mallinson said: "My thoughts are with the family of the person who died at this incredibly difficult time.

"Our inquiries are ongoing to establish the full circumstances of this crash, and it is vital we trace the three people who left the area before police arrived."

He asked anyone with information to contact Police Scotland .

The Scottish Ambulance Service (SAS) dispatched three ambulances, two special operations response teams, a paramedic response unit and a critical care paramedic.

The road was closed for a number of hours to allow an investigation to take place but reopened at 19:05.

articles.title: Houthis say Saudi strikes hit prison in Yemen
articles.summary: Yemen's Houthi militia reported fresh Saudi airstrikes on its positions in the north-west of the country, with 14 people killed or injured, according to Hout...
articles.body:
Houthi militia in Yemen reported fresh Saudi airstrikes in al-Jawf province, resulting in 14 casualties, including prisoners trapped under rubble.

Video footage released by the Houthis showed extensive damage to a prison hit in the attacks, with 35 inmates present at the time of the strike.

Yemeni government forces have announced a military operation to retake Houthi-controlled territory in al-Jawf, with clashes intensifying on multiple fronts in recent days.

Yemen's Houthi militia reported fresh Saudi airstrikes on its positions in the north-west of the country, with 14 people killed or injured, according to Houthi-controlled health authorities.

Saudi Arabia carried out airstrikes in al-Jawf province, the Iran-backed militia said. There was no comment from Riyadh.

A prison was also hit in the attacks, according to Houthi sources. Several inmates were taken to hospital, while others were believed to be trapped under the rubble.

There were 35 prisoners in the facility at the time of the strike, the sources said.

Video footage released by the Houthis showed extensive damage to parts of the building. The reports could not be independently verified.

The "Saudi aggression against Yemen" would not go unanswered, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said.

Fighting has been taking place between Yemeni government forces and the Houthis in al-Jawf. Government forces have announced a military operation aimed at retaking Houthi-controlled territory, with clashes intensifying on several fronts in recent days.

The Iran-backed Houthis have been fighting Yemen's Saudi-backed government for more than a decade.

An informal truce had largely held since 2022, but fighting in Yemen has flared up again in connection with the war involving Iran.

articles.title: Witkoff touts ‘substantive progress’ after peace talks with Ukraine, Russia
articles.summary: Special envoy Steve Witkoff touted “substantive progress” in the wake of U.S. talks on the Russia-Ukraine war with both sides. “United States negotiators visited both Moscow and Kyiv in order to facilitate additional dialogue to end the Russia-Ukraine War. Ahead of the trip, the Russians and Ukrainians agreed to a three-day no-shoot policy to enable…
articles.body:
Special envoy Steve Witkoff touted “substantive progress” in the wake of U.S. talks on the Russia-Ukraine war with both sides.

“United States negotiators visited both Moscow and Kyiv in order to facilitate additional dialogue to end the Russia-Ukraine War. Ahead of the trip, the Russians and Ukrainians agreed to a three-day no-shoot policy to enable these discussions to occur,” Witkoff said in a statement obtained by NewsNation’s Hannah Brandt.

“Special Envoy Witkoff, Jared Kushner, and officials from the National Security Council, State Department, and Treasury Department met with both President Putin of Russia and President Zelenskyy of Ukraine in order to discuss each side’s proposals with the other,” he added.

Witkoff added later in the statement that “substantive progress was made, including movement on scheduling additional trilateral talks.”

The war between Russia and Ukraine has been one of the main foreign policy problems dogging the U.S. in the last few years, and if the conflict continues past next February, it will cross the four-year mark.

On Sunday, Witkoff said the U.S. was confident that trilateral talks will lead to a “good resolution” to the war in Ukraine after he and Jared Kushner, President Trump’s son-in-law, met with officials in Kyiv.

According to CNN , Sunday was the envoys’ first time visiting Kyiv to negotiate an end to the war. Witkoff said in a press conference that their discussions were “substantive” and that he had confidence “that there’ll be a good resolution here.” Witkoff and Kushner met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday.

articles.title: Trump threatens to block Canada’s Bombardier sales unless planes made in US
articles.summary: Trump targets aeroplane maker again, accusing Canada of unfair practices and threatening to block sales in the US.
articles.body:
U‌nited States President Donald ⁠Trump has said that Canada-based aeroplane maker Bombardier can no longer sell in the US unless they start manufacturing their planes in the United States.

“NO MORE SELLING BOMBARDIER IN THE UNITED STATES! Their products aren’t good enough!” Trump said on Monday in a social media post. “If they want our Market, they must build here, and stop treating America like a ‘piggybank’.”

Trump’s comments come as tensions flare once again between the US and Canada, which have historically had tight relations. Trump has imposed a series of tariffs on Canadian products, prompting retaliatory actions. The retaliatory tariffs are set to take effect on early Tuesday.

The tariffs come as negotiations between the United States and Canada have deteriorated in recent weeks. Canada’s tariffs will cover nearly $20bn of 700 different US goods.

This is not the first time the US president has targeted Bombardier since returning to office in 2025.

Shares of Canadian aeroplane maker Bombardier plunged in January after Trump threatened to decertify the private jet maker’s large-cabin planes and slap 50 percent import tariffs on new planes until Canada certified the latest aircraft produced by US rival Gulfstream.

“Over 50% of their revenue comes from the United States — They live off American Buyers, American Companies, American Airports, and American Service,” Trump said on Monday. “Canada blocks our GREAT American Banks, and Companies, throughout the USA. They even blocked Gulfstream Aerospace from doing business in Canada — Completely unjust and unfair! That Era is OVER!”

The move will affect large private jet companies including NetJets, one of Bombardier’s biggest purchasers. In December 2023, the Columbus, Ohio-based company penned a deal with Bombardier to buy 12 Challenger 3500 jets outright, with Bombardier giving NetJets the option to buy up to another 232 aircraft later.

Bombardier did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

articles.title: Syria detains Assad-era general accused of bloody crackdown on protests
articles.summary: Major-General Mohammed Ali Durgham is accused of links to 1982 Hama massacre and 2011 protest crackdown.
articles.body:
Syrian authorities have announced the detainment of an Assad-era general accused of taking part in a massacre and overseeing a bloody crackdown on protests.

The country’s Internal Security Forces said on Monday that they had arrested former Major-General Mohammed Ali Durgham, who is accused of partaking in the Hama massacre in 1982 and ordering the shooting of unarmed protesters in 2011.

The detainment is the latest in a series of arrests as Syria’s government – led by figures from the former rebel group Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) that deposed former President Bashar Al-Assad in 2024 after decades of brutality – attempts to bring to justice those that ran his regime.

The statement labelled Durgham “a prominent officer in the military establishment during the era of the former regime”.

He is accused of being involved in “issuing direct order” to fire on unarmed protestors in the Damascus countryside.

Human Rights Watch in 2011 quoted a Syrian army defector who said that Durgham was one of the generals who “ordered the troops to shoot at protesters when his unit was deployed to areas in and just outside of Damascus”.

Durgham was a field commander in the army’s feared Fourth Division, commanded by Assad’s brother Maher al-Assad, between 2009 and 2013.

Durgham started “as a squad commander in the Defence Brigades during the events in Hama Governorate in 1982,” the authorities said.

On February 2, 1982, amid an information blackout, then-Syrian president Hafez al-Assad launched a brutal crackdown in the central Syrian city of Hama.

The death toll ranges from 10,000 to 40,000 people killed over the nearly month-long siege of the city.

Durgham’s arrest is part of broader efforts to pursue former officials accused of crimes and abuses under the previous regime.

Since Bashar al-Assad’s overthrow in December 2024, Syria’s new authorities have arrested dozens of former security officials.

Former Major-General Jalal Kamel Saqr was detained last week for his involvement in war crimes and arbitrary detentions, the state-run Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA) reported.

images.caption: A member of the former Syrian rebel group Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), which led the overthrow of former leader Bashar al-Assad, stands guard at the Fourth Division headquarters [File: Yamam Al Shaar/Reuters]

articles.title: The domestic armed threat facing Iran
articles.summary: External support for ethnic armed groups poses an escalating security threat to Iran, experts and state officials warn.
articles.body:
Iranian authorities have repeatedly publicised arrests and clashes with small armed cells inside the country, or skirmishes with armed groups along land borders, particularly in the lead-up to and during the war with Israel and the United States.

They have endeavoured to frame the war as a national security struggle while sending a message of control and deterrence to audiences inside the country and abroad.

In one of the latest instances, state media said on Sunday that members of an eight-member network allegedly affiliated with “anti-revolutionary” and “pro-monarchy” groups were arrested.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in the southern province of Fars accused those arrested of using Molotov cocktails and burning tyres during nationwide protests in January.

The leaders of Iran’s Islamic Republic have in recent weeks also expressed concern about more potential protests as public discontent rises amid deteriorating economic conditions.

During Iran’s January protests and on social media, a number of Iranians have expressed support for the return of the country’s monarchy, which was overthrown in the 1979 Islamic revolution.

Reza Pahlavi, the foreign-based son of Iran’s last shah, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, has been a leading opponent of the country’s government, and in January called on Iranians to join nationwide strikes and protests. Thousands are believed to have been killed during the unrest.

But even though there are instances of chanting in support of Pahlavi in Iran, there are currently no major organised pro-monarchy armed groups operating inside the country.

And while multiple nationwide demonstrations have swept Iran in recent years, they have largely been rooted in protesting economic grievances and repression in the country, rather than support for the monarchy.

US President Donald Trump, as well as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, did openly discuss the goal of overthrowing the Iranian state during the opening months of the war, which began in late February. Calls for the monarchy to replace the Islamic Republic have been particularly prominent in demonstrations outside of Iran.

The Iranian government has since then announced a large number of arrests of people it says are supporters of the monarchy.

That has included 111 so-called “monarchist cells” arrested across 26 provinces , as announced on March 18 by the Intelligence Ministry.

Iranian authorities consider the January protests a “coup” orchestrated by armed agents of the US and Israel, including pro-monarchists.

The United Nations and international rights groups have condemned state forces for the “brutality” shown during the crackdown on protesters.

The judiciary has executed dozens of prisoners since the start of the war, including some of those who protested in January. Numerous students, artists, businesspeople, journalists, healthcare workers and others have also been arrested over recent months for acts perceived by the authorities to be against national security.

Kurdish fighters active close to Iran’s western borders with Iraq are the country’s largest non-state armed threat.

Multiple groups, designated as “terrorist” outfits by Iranian authorities, have been based in the semiautonomous Kurdish region of northern Iraq for years.

Iran’s military forces have attacked bases operated by these groups in Iraq in recent years, while also pursuing security deals with the Iraqi government to contain them.

At the start of this year’s war, the Kurdish armed groups were considered by the Trump administration to lead a limited ground operation in western Iran to complement extensive air strikes by US and Israeli fighter jets and warships.

The Reuters news agency reported in early March that roughly 5,000-8,000 Iranian Kurdish fighters from groups including the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan (PDKI), and Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK) were preparing for a potential cross-border operation and had held discussions with US and Israeli representatives.

But the groups said they lacked sufficient weaponry and did not receive a clear signal from Washington to initiate the operation. The plan was not set into motion, and by April the IRGC had sent more troops to the border provinces.

Trump later repeatedly claimed that he had supplied arms to Kurdish forces, but that they had kept the weapons for themselves .

Aside from the Kurdish forces, Iran’s disenfranchised and restive southeastern border areas are also home to separatist Baloch fighters.

In late August, security forces said they had broken up a cell belonging to Jaish al-Adl, the most prominent of the Baloch armed groups. One rebel fighter was reported to have been killed, six arrested, and rifles, grenade launchers and explosives seized. But sporadic attacks from the group have been ongoing, at times killing police officers and IRGC figures.

Iranian authorities have said they will continue to bolster border control in order to limit exposure to armed groups amid the war.

Alex Vatanka, a senior fellow at the Washington-based Middle East Institute, said that external support for the Kurdish and Baloch rebel groups could increase the security challenge facing the authorities.

“The Iranian state might see any signs of increased external support for ethnic militants to be of an existential kind this time around due to the war situation,” he told Al Jazeera.

“I only see ethnic militant groups as possibly decisive [in the war] if they are part of a broader externally-funded push to pressure the regime in Tehran, which the Islamic Republic is already anticipating and calls a foreign-led hybrid-war campaign,” Vatanka added.

For his part, Trita Parsi, the Quincy Institute’s co-founder, said that while separatist militias don’t pose an existential threat to the government, they “may prove tremendously problematic for Tehran if the war with the US escalates after the mid-terms and the US decides, for instance, to deploy ground troops”

“If Trump decides to accept military risks after the midterms that he earlier eschewed, such as deploying ground troops, then it is highly conceivable that the US will seek to use armed militias inside the country,” Parsi added.

During the January protests, Trump and other US officials backed Iranian protesters and said they should continue to act with the goal of overthrowing the Islamic Republic.

Similar rhetoric from Washington has been heard since the start of the war.

Last week, Trump discussed the possibility that the pressure from war, sanctions and a naval blockade of Iran’s southern ports could ultimately lead to an internal uprising, or even the fall of the establishment.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the pressure could prompt Iranians to take to the streets again, or even create divisions within the IRGC.

“Maybe the people will rise up,” he said. “There is 100 percent inflation, queues, the military isn’t getting paid, [and] the central bank governor was in a panic last week.”

articles.title: Olivia Dunne pours beers like a patriot while her LSU tigers run up the score, Gator Bait & Lane's subtle shot
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin's LSU demolished Clemson as Olivia Dunne poured Miller Lites for fans, while Florida revived its controversial Gator Bait chant.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com. "The Week 1 college football schedule stinks, the NCAA needs to try a little harder next time!" Idiot. Goodness, I was an IDIOT Friday. That was my big gripe going into this glorious first weekend of college football. The schedule wasn't great. On paper, it wasn't. CLOCK CONTROVERSY ALLOWS MICHIGAN WOLVERINES TO AVOID MASSIVE UPSET AGAINST WESTERN MICHIGAN Of course, college football games are played on the field, and they never, ever disappoint. Simpletons like myself look at the paper and see "Western Michigan-Michigan" and think we're in for a snoozer. And then the Big Ten refs slap you across the face and tell you to SNAP OUT OF IT. What a game! What a weekend. And how about the Ole Miss-Louisville shootout from last night? How lucky are we? How great is college football. Welcome back, old friend. Let's have a season. Welcome to a Labor Day Nightcaps — the one where Olivia Dunne serves up booze while Lane Kiffin serves up an a–kicking to Clemson and poor Dabo Swinney. Lordy, what a mismatch. What else? I've got the Florida Gators reviving a lib-triggering chant, the field for last night's game in Nashville was disgraceful, and how great is the ESPN broadcasting team of Sean McDonough and Greg McIlroy? I said it last year, and I'll say it again today: If those two are on a call, expect fireworks. Every time. It never fails. OK, grab you one final summer beer before the unofficial calendar tuns to fall at 12 a.m., and settle in for a special holiday 'Cap! Olivia Dunne returned to LSU this weekend and served up some patriotism Look, it's a holiday. You're all (hopefully) grilling/drinking/both right now, and paying very little attention to this class. Trust me, I don't take it personally. Because of that, we're gonna keep it short and simple. We all have things to do and more football to watch. Lord knows I do. So, let's go ahead and get this Labor Day party started with Olivia Dunne returning to her roots and pouring some ice cold Miller Lites for the Tiger faithful before LSU absolutely annihilated Clemson on Saturday: Lane claps back OutKick pointed this out months ago, but it's worth repeating today: Miller Lite partnering with Livvy Dunne to promote their beer was the smartest move a beer company has made in quite some time. Look at the Bud Light fiasco from a few years back. I'm pretty sure Bud is still trying to recover. I'm not sure they ever fully will. Miller saw that, took some notes, used their brains, and decided to bring in Olivia Dunne this year instead. It worked out perfectly with Lane Kiffin going to LSU, too. Talk about a 1-2 punch! Speaking of Lane at LSU ... those with good hearing caught this little remark during his halftime interview of Saturday's blowout win against Clemson: Gator Bait, McDonough & is this field a joke? Amazing. Look, I'm no longer the biggest Lane Kiffin fan. I used to be, but the way he left Ole Miss last fall really turned me away. At this point, the proof is sort of in the pudding. He will, inevitably, leave things in terrible shape. Tennessee. USC. Oakland. Ole Miss. There will always be drama. That being said, he's still a #content machine. Fair is fair, and that was a funny little one-liner at the end. Sure, it's a little silly given he's the one choosing to create all this NFL-college drama, but if his team's gonna go into the locker room up 31-3 at the half, he's welcome to talk all the crap he'd like. And I'll eat it up. OK, let's rapid-fire this quick holiday class into a big Labor Day night. First? You know who is also a #content machine in the world of college football? New Florida coach Jon Sumrall. Look at what this DEMON brought back to Ben Hill Griffin Stadium on Saturday: Goodness, did I miss that song! I grew up going to Gators games during the glory years ('98-2011), and that song was such a banger every time. For those confused as to why the left deemed it racist ... The former UF president canceled it back in 2020 because of what he deemed racist imagery and literature from way back in the early 1900s. That imagery? Black children being used as bait to catch alligators. Yeah, disgusting. Not good. Also, not at all associated with the Gator Bait chant. Literally no correlation! "While I know of no evidence of racism associated with our ‘Gator Bait’ cheer at UF sporting events, there is horrific historic racist imagery associated with the phrase," former UF president Kent Fuchs wrote in a letter in June 2020. Still, he bent the knee because the world went absolutely crazy during that horrible summer, and the Gator Bait chant had been locked away ever since. Until this past weekend, when the fine folks in Gainesville dusted it off and unleashed it for the first time in six years. Perfection. Sanity wins again! Next? How great was Sean McDonough last night? I know Fowler and Herbie get all the shine, but I maintain that any time Sean McDonough is on the call for a college football game, it's destined to be electric: Sean McDonough, by the way, is the only announcer I can think of who excels in not one, not two, but THREE sports. He's a great baseball guy. I grew up listening to him call Red Sox games for WEEI, and he still does occasionally during the summer. Amazing. He's also ESPN's hockey guy, and he nails it. Obviously, he's done both college and the NFL. Don't forget, he took over for Tirico on Monday Night Football during a pretty down time for ESPN in terms of games. They used to get some pretty awful MNF games. That, of course, changed when Joe Buck and Troy Aikman came in a few years ago. Weird! My point? Sean McDonough probably deserves more praise than he gets. I'd put him up there with the best of the best. In terms of college football, there is no one better at the moment. Frankly, it's not close. OK, that's it for today. Good start to the week. Let's enjoy some football tonight. And Wednesday. And Thursday. And Friday. And Saturday. And Sunday. And again, next Monday! articles.title: Bovine TB: Gaps in evidence about impact of vaccinating badgers
articles.summary: Researchers want increased monitoring of the vaccination's impact on the disease and a review of the evidence.
articles.body:
There are "significant gaps" in knowledge and evidence about the effect of vaccinating badgers in Wales against bovine tuberculosis (TB), according to researchers.

A team from the British Ecological Society's Wales policy group, along with staff from Cardiff and Aberystwyth universities, argue the gaps reduce the effectiveness of this method of trying to deal with the disease.

Vaccination is part of a programme to eradicate bovine TB in Wales, but it is a controversial topic.

The Welsh government said it was "renewing" its approach to eradicating bovine TB.

There have been calls for alternative methods to vaccination for controlling the infection among cattle, such as badger culling, as they can carry the disease and transmit it to cattle.

Cattle are regularly tested for the presence of the infection and are slaughtered if they are found to be carriers.

The call for more monitoring comes in a new policy briefing by researchers.

They are calling for increased monitoring of the vaccination's impact, a review of the evidence, and collaboration with farmers "to ensure the greatest possible impact" from the programmes.

In their policy briefing, they say "major questions remain about how many badgers are being vaccinated, what impact vaccinating badgers is having on disease levels in cattle, and how confidence in vaccination can be improved among farmers and veterinary professionals".

Dr Niall McKeown, a lecturer in the department of life sciences at Aberystwyth University and vice-chair of the British Ecological Society's Wales policy group, said the infection "remains one of the biggest animal health challenges facing Wales".

"Badger vaccination should not be presented as a stand-alone route to eradicating bovine tuberculosis," said McKeown.

"There is strong evidence that BCG vaccination protects badgers, but evidence that operational vaccination programmes reduce disease in cattle remains limited.

"Any cattle-level benefit is likely to depend on sustained and sufficiently extensive vaccination coverage alongside effective cattle controls."

He emphasised it was not simply more vaccination that was needed "but vaccination that is better targeted, measured and evaluated".

"By combining non-invasive genetic monitoring with sett surveys, camera traps and movement data, we can estimate local badger numbers, check the proportion of the population reached and identify significant gaps," he added.

A spokesperson for the Welsh government said: "We are renewing our approach to eradicating bovine TB in Wales, focusing on three main elements: cattle, people, and wildlife.

"This work will be evidence-based and science-led, taking into account advice from the programme board and the technical advisory group, while ensuring that value for money remains a core consideration in decision-making."

Last month, Llyr Gruffydd, the minister responsible for agriculture, said there was a need to "look at a range of solutions".

He said the "picture varies from farm to farm" and that a "wide range of options" were being considered.

His comments came as the Welsh government announced the extension of two projects aiming to eradicate bovine TB.

The project began as a pilot scheme introduced in two areas - Pembrokeshire, where there is a very high number of TB cases, and parts of north Wales - but there was no intention to expand this to other areas.

In August 2024, a new board was established by the government to try to eliminate the disease.

articles.title: Book swap scheme turns Sunderland seafront into open-air library
articles.summary: Holidaymakers and locals are urged to borrow, exchange, or replace books in the Little Libraries.
articles.body:
Book lovers are being invited to combine a good read with a sea view after four Little Libraries sprang up along the coast.

The book cases have been installed on Sunderland seafront where holidaymakers and local people can borrow, exchange or replace a book.

The aim is to get visitors to enjoy reading by the sea by choosing one of the libraries' offerings, while at the same time giving a new home to books which might otherwise be gathering dust at home.

The Little Libraries have been set up at The Seaburn Inn, The Tram Shelter, Adventure Sunderland and the Marina by the city's Seafront Volunteer Group and Sunderland Seafront BID.

Each of the four cases has been turned into a one-off work of art by Su Devine, from Sunderland's Art Cafe, and the project has backing from the National Literacy Trust.

Roberta Redecke, head of business services at Sunderland BID, said the response so far had been "brilliant".

"People are really embracing the Little Libraries and finding them an incredibly useful way to take the opportunity to read against the backdrop of Sunderland's magnificent coastline," she said.

"It's a small but really effective way to make a visit to the seafront even more enjoyable and something everyone can take part in."

The launch ties in with 2026 being the National Year of Reading - a UK-wide push to get more people discovering the pleasure of reading.

A Look For the Book treasure hunt between Roker and Seaburn, with copies hidden along the route for visitors to find and keep, will take place on 3 October.

articles.body: Passengers aboard a cruise ship preparing to set sail for Alaska were left scrambling recently after the cruise line abruptly canceled the trip — citing unspecified technical problems. The seven-night Alaska cruise aboard Royal Caribbean’s Serenade of the Seas was scheduled to depart Vancouver, Canada, on Aug. 30 but had been delayed until Sept. 1 for maintenance, according to the blog "Cruise Critic." But the trouble didn't end there. Some two days after passengers embarked in Vancouver, Royal Caribbean reportedly announced that the voyage aboard Serenade of the Seas was canceled. CRUISES THROWN INTO CHAOS AS DROUGHT STRANDS SHIPS, LEAVES PASSENGERS SCRAMBLING Passengers were able to use the ship’s amenities as they worked on booking flights home, several cruise blogs reported. The voyage was originally scheduled to stop in Sitka, Juneau, Ketchikan and Prince Rupert. "To accommodate ongoing maintenance, we’ve had to cancel our sailing. We apologize to our guests for the inconvenience and have worked with them to adjust their travel plans," a Royal Caribbean Group spokesperson told Fox News Digital in a shared statement. "Repairs have now been completed, and the ship is ready to welcome guests on its next scheduled sailing," the spokesperson added. The problem started on Aug. 22. Royal Caribbean emailed guests to inform them that the sailing would be reduced to five days to accommodate additional maintenance, "Cruise Critic" reported. The ship is known for its floor-to-ceiling windows that offer views of the surrounding scenery. Guests who weren't interested in the shortened trip were given several options, including a refundable onboard credit and a future cruise credit, according to the blog. The ship ultimately did not leave Vancouver because the repairs were not finished, the blog said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER All booked passengers will receive a full refund, retain their previously issued onboard credit, receive a future cruise credit for 100% of their cruise fare and receive reimbursement for eligible flight-change fees, the "Royal Caribbean Blog" reported. Serenade of the Seas, a mid-sized Royal Caribbean vessel, can accommodate 2,143 guests at double occupancy. The ship is known for its floor-to-ceiling windows that offer views of the surrounding scenery, alongside amenities like a rock-climbing wall, a glass-domed solarium and multiple dining venues. The ship has experienced other technical difficulties in recent years. In July 2025, Serenade of the Seas experienced engine trouble soon after leaving Vancouver for a seven-night Alaska cruise, forcing it to return to port for overnight testing, several publications reported. The vessel set sail again the following evening, but passengers missed out on a planned stop in Sitka, Alaska. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Days earlier, technical problems on the ship's June 29 sailing had caused it to skip Icy Strait Point and scenic cruising in Tracy Arm Fjord, with those passengers receiving onboard credit equal to one day of their cruise fare. Some passengers affected by the canceled Alaska cruise took to Reddit to express their frustration. "This has been an immense disappointment. This was my girlfriend’s birthday cruise with my family and some family friends, and it has been an utter disaster and disappointment from start to finish," a Reddit user said. "I was told [to] feel free to use my onboard credits on the ship — but for what? Only a few of the bars are open. None of the shops or casinos [are] open," a Reddit user said in another thread. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "Oh my, what a disaster. Glad I canceled and didn’t board. Still waiting for my cruise fare refund, though," said another person. Several online commenters expressed sympathy for those inconvenienced by the cancellation, while others expressed apprehension about future trips they've booked with the line. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP One Reddit user asked what a group of eight can "absolutely not miss in Vancouver" as they planned to "enjoy the rest of the week and keep our flights home." Serenade of the Seas welcomed passengers aboard again on Sept. 6 for its next seven-day, round-trip Alaska cruise, the "Royal Caribbean Blog" reported on Sept. 7.

articles.title: UK government refuses slavery reparations as Jamaica urges king to act
articles.summary: Britain expresses sorrow over slavery, but rejects financial compensation.
articles.body:
The United Kingdom’s government has reiterated that it rejects reparations for Britain’s role in the transatlantic slave trade as Jamaica has petitioned King Charles III over the issue.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s spokesperson said on Monday that “the UK does not and will not pay reparations”.

Successive British governments have refused to engage in discussions about slavery reparations, while accepting that the country significantly benefitted from the trade.

UK leaders have previously acknowledged the horrors of slavery and continue to do so, but have never formally apologised for Britain’s role in sustaining it.

Burnham’s spokesperson labelled the practice as “abhorrent”, but maintained that position and insisted no compensation will be paid.

A delegation led by Jamaican Culture Minister Olivia Grange delivered a petition to Buckingham Palace on Monday, asking King Charles to seek legal advice from the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London.

The petition poses three questions for the king to consider: whether the enslavement of Africans in Jamaica was legal under English law; whether it violated international law; and whether the UK has a legal obligation to provide compensation for the harms caused by slavery.

The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council is the final court of appeal for Jamaica and some other Commonwealth countries and territories.

The Jamaican delegation is seeking $10bn in reparations and says it is the first time a Commonwealth country has tried to use this legal route.

King Charles is currently in Scotland and was not present at the palace as the petition was delivered.

“Once again Charles ducks for cover when the issue of slavery and empire is raised,” said Graham Smith, CEO of anti-monarchy campaign group Republic.

Minister Grange is also seeking the return of Caribbean artefacts held in British museums. Despite the king’s absence, and the government’s reiteration that reparations will not be paid, Grange told the Reuters news agency that she was “encouraged”.

Last month, a United Nations committee concluded that countries are legally obliged to consider slavery reparations, warning that racial discrimination could not be tackled without “a full commitment to review and redress the ongoing harms and consequences of the trafficking of enslaved Africans and racialised slavery”.

articles.title: At 16, an Indiana girl earned 5 cents a day working at a neighbourhood café; her family later bought it, and 100 years after it opened her daughter still runs it
articles.summary: US News: When 16-year-old Frances began washing dishes and serving customers at a neighbourhood eatery along the St. Joseph River in South Bend, Indiana, she e.
articles.body: When 16-year-old Frances began washing dishes and serving customers at a neighbourhood eatery along the St. Joseph River in South Bend, Indiana, she earned just five cents a day. A century later, the same restaurant is still in her family, serving its famous hand-rolled meatballs and red sauce that is simmered for two days. Celebrating its 100th anniversary in 2026, the Sunny Italy Cafe is South Bend’s oldest operating restaurant, with Frances’s daughter now running the kitchen and dining room. According to reporting by Bluewater Healthy Living and an archival feature from Yahoo News, the restaurant’s story began in 1926 when Anthony and Rose Vumbaca opened a cafe at 601 North Niles Avenue, originally called the North Niles Avenue Cafe. Frances, who lived across the street, started working there soon after it opened to help support her family. In 1940, her parents, Jimmy and Josie Bamber, bought the business from the Vumbacas and officially renamed it the Sunny Italy Cafe. Even after the name changed, generations of local customers and nearby University of Notre Dame students continued to call the restaurant "Rosie’s", in honour of its original co-founder.Feeding generations of Notre Dame studentsBy the late 1930s and 1940s, the cafe had become an important part of the South Bend community and the nearby university campus. Archives kept by the University of Notre Dame show that hundreds of students would walk through snow and strong winds along North Niles Avenue every Friday and Saturday night, forming long queues that stretched onto the street. To handle the growing crowds, the Bamber family expanded the dining room in 1947, increasing seating to 150 guests. The restaurant focused heavily on student customers, offering affordable lunch and dinner specials while staying open late on weekends when students went to the movies. Over the years, the cafe hosted political banquets, fraternity dinners and alumni gatherings. Figures including former Democratic National Committee chairman Paul Butler and Republican Congressman Melvin Laird spoke to student groups inside the restaurant during the 1950s and 1960s. A 1976 feature in Notre Dame’s Scholastic magazine said university students made up about 40 per cent of the cafe’s business. This helped create a family tradition in which former students returned with their children and grandchildren.Scratch cooking keeps the tradition aliveThe restaurant’s long success is closely linked to cooking methods that have stayed almost unchanged since the 1920s. Every sauce is made from scratch, salad dressings are prepared fresh in-house each day, and meats are prepared by hand using family recipes passed down through generations. The kitchen still spends up to two full days simmering its main ragù and red sauces before serving them with handmade ravioli and manicotti. Fresh bread is still supplied by Gonnella Baking Company, a Chicago-based bakery that has also been operating for more than a century. Today, Frances’s daughter manages daily operations at the 601 North Niles Avenue location. She has kept its dim lighting, vintage booths and historic photographs covering the wood-panelled walls. "Sunny Italy Cafe provides a historic take on classic Italian cuisine," noted local historical coverage by Bluewater Healthy Living, pointing out how rare it is for an independent American restaurant to remain under family ownership for a full century. Instead of changing with modern food trends, the restaurant continues to offer a focused menu featuring broiled chicken, house-made sausage and veal parmigiana. As it begins its second century beside the St. Joseph River, the former North Niles Avenue Cafe continues to attract nightly crowds, serving as a living time capsule of South Bend’s culinary history.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Judge Sandeep Mehta has written another letter to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant alleging that Rajasthan high court judge .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Judge Sandeep Mehta has written another letter to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant alleging that Rajasthan high court judge Sanjeev Prakash Sharma, who was replaced as the Acting Chief Justice of Rajasthan high court, was interfering in an internal judicial enquiry by abusing administrative powers.This is the fourth letter written by Justice Mehta to CJI on the conduct of the Rajasthan HC judge. His earlier three letters on Aug 2, 10 and 17 had accused Justice Sharma, the then Acting Chief Justice of Rajasthan HC, of "maladministration", "malpractices", "nepotism" and "favouritism". The letter triggered protest from a lawyer in HC and saw the Supreme Court collegium recommending Justice Sanjay K Agrawal's name as Chief Justice of Rajasthan high court, which was approved by the central govt.Justice Mehta had pleaded for the transfer of Justice Sharma, who is retiring on Sept 26, and appointment of a regular chief justice. Justice Mehta also complained as to why CJI Surya Kant had not acted on his fervent pleas.In his fourth letter, Justice Mehta said that he has "further information" and "material" regarding arbitrary, dubious and patently "high-handed" acts of Justice Sharma.Referring to a complaint committee of high court which was constituted to enquire into allegations against a judicial officer accused of displaying indecent pictures of a fellow woman officer on his mobile phone, Justice Mehta said, "Two Resolutions of the committee dated May 21, 2026, and July 9, 2026, clearly record that the Acting Chief Justice (Justice Sharma) has made direct intervention in the enquiry proceedings, hampering the independence of the committee and that such intervention could vitiate the enquiry as a whole and also breached the confidentiality of such sensitive proceedings.""The committee also observed that the Acting Chief Justice caused records of the committee to be shared with other officers of the registry and judicial officers, thereby breaching the confidentiality of the enquiry instituted against a judicial officer with grave charges," he claimed.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Indiana farm vows to ‘absolutely’ do Charlie Kirk corn maze again despite wave of backlash
articles.summary: Global Farms says critics flooded its Google reviews with one-star ratings after unveiling the Charlie Kirk corn maze, but worldwide support followed.
articles.body: An Indiana family farm facing backlash over a massive corn maze honoring Charlie Kirk says it has no regrets about the tribute and would "absolutely" do it again, telling Fox News Digital that critics began hammering the business with one-star reviews almost immediately after the design was unveiled. Jeremy Goebel, a manager at family-owned Global Farms, said the farm never intended for the maze to be divisive, but wanted to remember Kirk and his advocacy for open debate and free speech. "Absolutely, we would absolutely do it again," Goebel said. "And although, you know, this is just pushback and negative commentary on us, I don't really feel like it's directed at us. I mean, sure, people are saying. It's about us, but it's really about Charlie. They have the issue with what he stood for." HOW CHARLIE KIRK INSPIRED HIS MENTOR'S FIGHT TO DEFEND REALITY The Turning Point USA was assassinated Sept. 10, 2025, while speaking at Utah Valley University during his "American Comeback Tour." Goebel said the backlash began the same day the farm announced the maze, with some people, including previous customers, leaving one-star reviews because they opposed the tribute. BUFFALO MUSIC VENUE BANS DJ AFTER 'WE ARE CHARLIE KIRK' SONG PLAYED IN JEST "Unfortunately, the first day that we had announced it, people began giving us one-star reviews, even some previous customers, because they posted their photos with their one-star review, simply because they disagreed with the corn maze," Goebel said. "And so we got a message from Google saying that someone had said that we were doing deceptive practices, and so they closed the profile, at least temporarily until we have a chance to appeal it." For Goebel, the backlash has been hard to understand. HE FLED COMMUNISM. NOW THIS CALIFORNIA MAYOR IS HONORING CHARLIE KIRK AND REFUSING TO BACK DOWN "I just think it's very hard to wrap my mind around the fact that there's been so much hate over this, we were just trying to remember a man who lost his life promoting freedom of speech," Goebel said. "I know not everybody agrees with him, and I'm not saying that we agreed with everything, and I'm not saying that we disagreed with everything, but, we just wanted to remember someone who lost their life for the cause of free speech and to get people educated." But the response has not been all negative, Goebel said. ERIKA KIRK URGES CONSERVATIVE STUDENTS NOT TO BACK DOWN IN FIRST SCHOOL YEAR SINCE CHARLIE'S ASSASSINATION "We've received a lot of backlash over the last few days, but especially that first day, the last 24 hours, I would say the majority is positive, actually," Goebel said. "Actually, I've heard from people all over the world, from Cape Town, South Africa, and even Australia, actually, in support of it. So I think it was never intended to be divisive. It was only just to remember Charlie, because obviously he lost his life." He said the country would do better to listen more to each other. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE "I think part of what makes America great is that we can challenge each other’s ideas and disagree," Goebel told Fox News Digital. "No one side has all the answers, and I think a lot of our best ideas and progress come from people with different perspectives pushing each other to think differently. We probably accomplish more as a society when we’re willing to listen to each other instead of just assuming the other side is wrong." articles.title: Trump posts map with American flag emblazoned over Canada, Greenland, Mexico
articles.summary: President Trump posted a map with an American flag covering most of North America, as well as Iceland and islands in the Caribbean, on Monday morning, a post that follows his previous pushes to take over territory outside of U.S. borders. The president’s post featured a map with the pattern of the American flag superimposed…
articles.body:
President Trump posted a map with an American flag covering most of North America, as well as Iceland and islands in the Caribbean, on Monday morning, a post that follows his previous pushes to take over territory outside of U.S. borders.

The president’s post featured a map with the pattern of the American flag superimposed over the U.S., Canada, Mexico and part of Central America, as well as Greenland, Iceland and islands in the Caribbean such as Cuba and Jamaica.

Trump has previously pushed to take over Canada and Greenland, as well as the Panama Canal, but the inclusion of countries like Mexico and some of the Caribbean islands in his territorial ambitions is new.

The post also comes amid U.S. tensions with Canada over trade, with Washington and Ottawa slapping tariffs on each other’s goods in the last month. Amid the trade troubles between the U.S. and its northern neighbor, Trump signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario, which shares a name with a Canadian province, to “Lake America.”

On Sunday , Trump posted a map of New Mexico labeled “New America” after a debunked online hoax spread that he had signed an executive order changing the state’s name.

The map, which the president posted to Truth Social, featured a large “X” over “Mexico” in the state’s name and the word “America” below it. The White House’s official account also posted the image on the social platform X.

articles.title: Passive smoking deaths up 50% since 1990: Lancet
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Deaths linked to second-hand smoke in India have soared, surging almost 50% since 1990 and claiming 325,600 lives in 2023 alone. According .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Deaths linked to second-hand smoke in India have soared, surging almost 50% since 1990 and claiming 325,600 lives in 2023 alone. According to a study published in The Lancet Public Health Monday, India had the world's second-highest number of people exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, after China, with 444 million Indians affected.While India's age-standardised exposure prevalence declined from 43.2% to 30.6% over the last three decades, the absolute number of people exposed rose from 375 million in 1990 to 444 million in 2023, an increase of 18.4%. The health toll also rose sharply, with deaths attributable to second-hand smoke climbing from 217,700 to 325,600 during the same period.Fatalities among women rose from 113,400 to 156,900, while deaths among men from 104,300 to 168,700 over the same period. Second-hand smoke also accounted for 9.28 million disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) in India in 2023, representing healthy years lost to premature death, illness or disability.Dr G C Khilnani, chairperson of pulmonary, critical care at PSRI Hospital, said, "Second-hand smoke contributes not only to illness and disability but also to premature deaths and loss of healthy years. Kids and women are particularly vulnerable, with children's developing lungs making them more susceptible to respiratory issues. Smoking should be done outdoors, and greater public awareness is needed."The study links second-hand smoke to ischaemic heart disease, stroke, lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, breast cancer, type 2 diabetes, asthma and lower respiratory infections. Among children, lower respiratory infections were the leading contributor to the disease burden.Globally, 2.71 billion people were exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, contributing to 1.66 million deaths and 44.8 million DALYs. China, India and Indonesia accounted for nearly half of world's exposed population, with China recording 664 million exposed people.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
